clue.text: Excuse offered by a worker in crafty but in affable fashion

parts.note: an excuse offered is a plea

indicators.note: the worker is placed inside the word for crafty, as the clue says it is in it

parts.note: crafty means sly
a worker is an ant, the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Someone's apology was cunning yet delivered with charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' and 'offered by' are only joining words; 'in affable fashion' is an adverb phrase, matching the -LY ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something pleasantly means doing it in a friendly, agreeable manner.

clue.text: Wooded walk?

parts.note: a walk that is heavy and wooden, like a plodding gait, while the word also means cut timber

explanation.definitionFit: To lumber is to move heavily and clumsily, and lumber is also sawn timber, hence the wooden pun.

clue.text: The renegade given a job scoffed

parts.note: a job is a post
scoffed in the sense of gobbled food means ate

explanation.surface: A traitor is rewarded with a position and mocked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' looks like mocked, but here it means ate greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade abandons a faith or cause, which is exactly what an apostate does.

clue.text: Charming and sober artist working outside

indicators.note: the word for working goes round the other pieces, standing outside them

parts.note: an actor at work is acting
TT means teetotal, so sober
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An engaging teetotal painter is busy at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts ACTING around TTRA, splitting it as A-TTRA-CTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charming is alluring, drawing people towards it.

clue.text: Ends in a much better minimum pay deal

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words better minimum, spanning the gap between them

parts.words: a much better minimum pay deal

explanation.surface: A union boasts its pay deal will greatly improve the minimum wage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals letters lurking in the words, here across 'better minimum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are terminal points, the places where lines or routes finish.

clue.text: Mundane period of revolution

parts.note: mundane in its old sense of earthly: the time the Earth takes to go round the sun, not a political uprising

explanation.definitionFit: A year is the time our planet takes for one orbit of the sun.

clue.text: Support a point put concerning an ambassador

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
a tine is a prong or point of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: Someone backs a proposal raised about a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: A legate is a papal envoy; LEGATINE is its adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Legatine describes things belonging to a legate, the Pope's envoy or emissary.

clue.text: A driver set out to be a promoter

indicators.note: set out suggests something rearranged or laid out afresh, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A motorist sets off with the aim of becoming a salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertiser promotes goods or services to the public.

clue.text: Out of cash to finish pay out

parts.note: ex means out of or from, as in ex works
P is a penny, a small piece of cash
finish means end

explanation.surface: Someone is broke at the end of the pay period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of cash' looks like one phrase meaning broke, but it splits into EX and P.
explanation.definitionFit: To expend money is to spend it, paying it away.

clue.text: Sense hesitation in a foreign dealer

parts.note: sense in the meaning of significance is import
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone senses reluctance in an overseas trader.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer is a merchant who buys goods from abroad, so a trader in overseas wares.

clue.text: Recipe for a soaking

parts.note: not a forecast of rain but a mixture of oil, wine and spices in which meat is steeped

explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is the seasoned liquid food is steeped in before cooking.

clue.text: A yard in extent

definitions.meaning: in Britain the sunken courtyard in front of a basement is called by this name
extent in the sense of size or measure of surface

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sunken basement courtyard and the size of a surface.

clue.text: Mugs people in the street — a charge results

parts.note: mugs are fools, asses

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
people means men

explanation.surface: Muggings by street gangs lead to someone being charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mugs' looks like a verb about robbery; it is the noun meaning fools.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a levy or tax imposed, a charge to be paid.

clue.text: After study a high-principled man accepts school check

parts.note: to con is to study, as in con a text

indicators.note: the saint takes in the other word, so it goes inside

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: After revision, a moral teacher allows the school an inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun but it is the verb meaning to train.
explanation.definitionFit: A constraint is a restraint or limit, something that holds back.

clue.text: A ruse cunningly used in efforts to make lots of money

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are put to use within the word for efforts

parts.note: efforts are tries

indicators.note: cunningly suggests a crafty rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A trick is deployed in schemes to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly' signals the anagram and 'used in' the insertion; 'lots of money' fits because treasuries hold great sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasuries are stores of wealth, so large stocks of funds.

clue.text: Changing month-end prices round

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters alter their order

parts.note: the last letter of month is H

explanation.surface: Prices fluctuate around the end of each month.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheric is an old form of spherical, meaning globe-shaped.

clue.text: Seafood at one time difficult to pin down

parts.note: difficult means hard
to tack is to fasten down with a pin

explanation.surface: Fish that was once hard to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardtack is hard ship's biscuit, the sailors' staple of old: food at sea rather than fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardtack was the dry biscuit eaten by sailors on long voyages, literally food at sea.

clue.text: Discourage the production of French publications

parts.note: de is French for of
the press is the body of newspapers and publications

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop French newspapers being published.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress is to dishearten or lower someone's spirits.

clue.text: A mender of broken marriages?

parts.note: read as one who pairs people off again, though the word really means anyone who fixes things

explanation.definitionFit: A repairer is a mender; split as re-pairer it suggests one who couples people afresh.

clue.text: This could well bring a guy down to earth!

definitions.text: This could well bring a guy down to earth!

parts.words: This could well bring a guy down to earth!
parts.note: guy is not a man but a rope steadying a tent, fixed to the ground by a peg

explanation.definitionFit: A tent peg anchors a guy rope in the ground.

clue.text: They put the squeeze on aliens holding money

indicators.note: the word for aliens contains the letter for money, holding it inside

parts.note: aliens are strangers
L is the abbreviation for a pound, money

explanation.surface: Foreigners with cash are being pressured.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranglers throttle their victims, literally squeezing their necks.

clue.text: River gold is low-grade

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A prospector finds the river's gold is of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Something low-grade is inferior in quality.

clue.text: Striking tennis —- and that's only the start

parts.note: workers on strike are out
a set is a unit of play in a tennis match

explanation.surface: A tennis strike is said to be merely the beginning of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests hitting the ball; it means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the beginning of something.

clue.text: A driver to the right — one in the majority

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for the majority

parts.note: the majority means most
R is the abbreviation for right
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A political driver of the right is in the majority.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is someone who drives a car.

clue.text: Innovative time piece

indicators.note: something innovative is new and different, so the letters are made anew in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A ground-breaking new timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time piece' looks like a clock; 'Innovative' rearranges TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single article or piece among several.

clue.text: Plain words about a border plant

indicators.note: the plain words go round the border word, being about it

parts.note: prose is plain, unversified writing
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Someone talks simply about a flower in a garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a flowerbed, tempting it into the definition, but it gives the edge word; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A primrose is a pale yellow spring-flowering wild plant.

clue.text: Woman rejecting places in the north-east

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the abbreviation for north-east

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-east

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the word for places is read backwards

parts.note: loci is the plural of locus, a place

explanation.surface: A woman spurns places in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' signals the reversal and 'in' the container; Nicole is simply a female first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicole is a girl's given name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: A real trier can be reduced to a grim state

indicators.note: reduced suggests broken down and reassembled, so the letters can be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: An earnest striver can end up in a grim condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A real trier' sounds like a hard worker, but means one who really tries cases in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a judge in a lower court, who genuinely hears and tries cases.
